predecessors.note: The Cocom, nearly annihilated at Mayapan in 1441, survive as lords of Sotuta.

capitals.name: Sotuta
capitals.note: The Kuchkabal page lists Sotuta as the capital; no coordinates on any page: the point is the researcher's geographic knowledge.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (no Cliopatria row). The Sotuta page is a stub with no extent; the conquest page says only 'landlocked, north of Maní'. Drawn as a 40 km disc at Sotuta, soft.

region.text: Sotuta, the Cocom province, 'landlocked, north of Maní'; the pages give no extent

ledger.note: 1441: 'all of the Cocom family, except one who was away in Honduras conducting trade, were killed' at Mayapan; the Cocom are later the lords of Sotuta, 'implacable enemies of the European colonisers' (conquest page). Neither page dates the province's founding, so 1441 is a bridge.

region.text: Sotuta, the Cocom province, 'landlocked, north of Maní'; the pages give no extent

ledger.note: 1545: 'Nachi Cocom, colonial governor of Sotuta' (Kuchkabal page), so the province is under Spanish rule by 1545; the conquest page has the Sotuta Cocom resisting until then (they joined the 1542 assault on Mérida).

wars.name: Allied assault on Mérida
wars.outcome: The Kuchkabal page has an alliance of Cupul, Cochuah and Sotuta in 'their allied assault on Spanish forces at Mérida in 1542'; the outcome is not stated.
wars.note: Hocabá, Chakan and the Xiu are not named in the alliance.

sources.title: Kuchkabal
sources.note: Provinces of Yucatan with capitals; 1542 allied assault on Mérida (Cupul, Cochuah, Sotuta); 1545 Nachi Cocom; 1557 Mani treaty; extents debated.

sources.title: Spanish conquest of Yucatán
sources.note: Province neighbours; Montejo 1527; Campeche 1531; retreat 1534/35; Campeche and Mérida councils 1541-42; late 1546 uprising of eastern provinces.

sources.title: Mayapan
sources.note: Xiu revolt 1441; Cocom killed; 'Yucatan devolved into warring city-states'.

sources.title: Sotuta
sources.note: A stub with no dates; only 'before the arrival of the Spanish conquistadors in the sixteenth century'.

notes: NEW STATE. Cliopatria has no row for this province; Later Mayan City-States (1429-1546, 135,136 to 187,745 km2) covers the whole northern lowlands and contains it. The Kuchkabal page says the extent of the provinces 'is still debated' and that scholars disagree 'on whether they were territorial units or jurisdictions'; the shape here is a disc around the capital, soft, and no frontier is claimed. Cliopatria keeps its envelope to 1546 although the Spanish took the provinces one by one from 1527. SOTUTA. The Sotuta page is a stub; every event rests on the Mayapan, Kuchkabal and conquest pages. Gazetteer lacks 'Sotuta'.
